utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning to everybody. As you can see, we are sitting with three Judges again. Yesterday we decided to have an extended sitting today. The proposal of the Registry was we have the three sessions until 1.45, and then three-quarters of an hour lunch break, and then again from 2.30 to 4.00 in the afternoon for the last full session. If there is an agreement, we will proceed like that. The witness should be brought in, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Good morning, sir. Please sit down and make yourself comfortable. I have to remind you that the affirmation to tell the truth still applies. Mr. Tolimir is now commencing his cross-examination. Mr. Tolimir, you have the floor.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Peace unto this house, and may this day in court and the final judgement reflect God's will and not necessarily mine. I wish the witness a pleasant sojourn amongst us, and I also offer my condolences. I didn't know that his mother had died. I'll do my best to finish today so that he may be able to travel home. And I kindly ask everybody to be as brief as possible so that we may, indeed, finish today. Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise for this introduction. And I would like to point out to you, Mr. Obradovic, that since we speak the same language, do follow the transcript. And once the cursor stops, then you may start with your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We'll start with what you remember, and I would like to display document -- I don't know which document it is. It was the last document, 65 ter 7298, about chemical weapons. That was the last one yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is now P2155.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] we can see it, but it's barely legible. That's why I will read out the portion of the document about which I'll ask my question. Please take a look at -- now we can't see it like this. Please return to the first view. Actually, we don't have to read at all. This says that I requested for chemicals, in my document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Perhaps it is possible that the Prosecution would give a hard copy of the B/C/S version of this document to the witness. That would help him to read it with the full text. And most of the text we have read -- or Mr. McCloskey has read into the transcript yesterday. Perhaps you can save some time not to do it again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. In that case, let us please see P488 so that the witness may be able to see all information to which this document of the Prosecution refers. We'll get back to this document later. Now we can see the document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please take a look at the paragraph starting with -- the paragraph after paragraph 4. It would -- or, rather: "The most propitious means of their destruction would be to use chemical weapons or aerosol grenades and bombs. By using these means, we would accelerate the surrender of Muslims and the fall of Zepa." This is what this document says, and it was sent to the Main Staff. Here's my question: Is the term used "chemical means" or "chemical weapons"? Please re-read what I have just read out.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The language used is "chemical means."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Are all chemical means considered chemical weapons; do you know that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please point out the difference between chemical means and chemical weapons to us, if you know, since you did not use any, but you may have some knowledge from school.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure, but I think that chemical weapons include means that are used at longer ranges and by artillery pieces or aircraft.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us, do chemical weapons have certain effects on those against whom they are used, whereas these chemical means do not have longstanding effects?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These bombs mentioned under 3 are hand-thrown. Actually, these grenades are hand-thrown, and they have only a short time effect. They're filled with tear gas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you for mentioning this. My legal assistant complained several times yesterday about the terminology used in the interpretation, "mine" versus "grenade." Can you comment on that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ... please slow down and do make a break between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, both speakers are overlapping very much again. Please pause between question and answer. Go ahead, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise both to the witness and you. I was hurrying.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yesterday, during the examination-in-chief, this B/C/S term "mina" [phoen] was interpreted into English as "grenade." Did you yesterday speak about shells or about grenades?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The B/C/S term "mina" in this context was correctly interpreted as "grenade" into English. Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would like to ask the witness to look on the screen where we have the record. You can see if this -- it is still moving, then the interpretation has not stopped. And, therefore, please start only with your answer when the interpretation and the recorder has stopped. Could you please repeat your last answer. It was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, yesterday I used the term "grenade" and the term "bomb." I did not use the term "shell." And I explained that shells are fired from artillery pieces.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Speaking about the correction of terminology, on page 69 of yesterday's transcript you spoke about weapons. And what was recorded in the transcript was the combat arms organ. Did you speak about a weapons organ?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If your question refers to what I spoke about regarding the organisational structure of the staff, I spoke about the combat arms organ, which means every combat arm had its organ in the staff sector. In other words, there was an infantry organ, an artillery organ, an armour and mechanised units organ, an APC protection organ, engineers organ, et cetera.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So you spoke about organs in charge of the combat arms, which was interpreted as organs in charge of weapons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise, but I must intervene. The term "combat arms" is used again. I believe that "branches" would be a more correct interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We are, as you know, Mr. Gajic, in the hands of the interpreters. But we have the tape, and that can be checked at a later stage. Please continue, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could we now see Exhibit P2155. We up-loaded it to e-court this morning because after the end of our session yesterday the Prosecutor provided us the document. The reference is 2155.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: P2155. It is the document we had on the screen at the beginning of this session, and the witness has a hard copy of it. I think it's not the right document. Now it is appearing. Mr. Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I didn't want this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- we have it on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now we're interested in item 3, "Special hand-grenade M-79 AG-1." We also have a picture of this hand-grenade, so we can show it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber what a hand-grenade is and how it is used? Please take a look at the picture first before you reply. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic, I would like to have the answer first, and then you may give your comment on the interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you've ever seen a defence hand-grenade and what that is?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: A defence hand-grenade -- or, rather, a hand-grenade can be either a defensive or an offensive hand-grenade. This is a special hand-grenade, M-79 AG-1. Military police units were armed with these hand-grenades for special procedures in riot control, in assault actions, and in order to render enemy forces' combat incapable.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We'll have a picture that we can provide to the OTP and the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, since the document was submitted late last night, we were unable to up-load it to e-court. But we have a photograph of the hand-grenade, and perhaps we can put it on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, we should do that, with the assistance of the Court Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Usher.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We see in front of us a special hand-grenade M-79 AG-1. The information about it is in English, but you will see that it was manufactured in the Trajal factory in Krusevac. You will see that in the second paragraph. And you will also see that it uses CS-1 gas and that it was used by the police. Would you say that it is an offensive or defensive weapon if it was used by the police in peacetime?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Its effects do not pertain to wartime activities. The effects are for special tasks that are usually carried out by the police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As you can see in the information, there's everything about that grenade here. Do you know that this grenade, filled by the so-called CS-1 gas, which is mixed with a pyrotechnical mass that we call tear gas?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm aware and familiar with the term "tear gas."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We could then say, for the benefit of us lay persons, that this gas is tear gas. This is its popular name. Do you know whether this grenade was used for riot control, for controlling football fans, in peacetime? Was it used by the police for those purposes?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Please, could we look at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, will you use this photograph again? And my second question: Are you tendering it as a document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I would like to tender this document into evidence. And now we are going to use another document, and we will remove this photo from the ELMO. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The first photograph will be received as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D200, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now we have a second photograph on the screen, -- on the ELMO. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And now we can see something on the screen, which is a rifle grenade and its technical characteristics. In the Prosecutor's document, it is called "M-83." Please, do you know what the composition of the rifle grenade is, SK M-83, a grenade that you can see on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is filled with the same type of agent, i.e., tear gas.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is this: Do you know whether tear gas falls under the category of aerosols?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you ever heard of those little sprays that women carry in their purses to protect themselves from attacks?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you perhaps know that these protection devices are filled with aerosol? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know whether we could use the term "aerosol," but I think I know what you mean, and the answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would it be the same aerosol that is used in riot control or in controlling football fans at football games by all the police forces of the world? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. But those sprays contain a lower quantity of the agent.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Would the group of chemical compounds that the Prosecutor spoke about yesterday belong to the group of lethal or non-lethal chemical agents? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They are non-lethal agents, and they have only temporary effect.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Are they then combat agents or non-combat agents?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Non-combat.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you said, on page 9, line 6 and 7: "In the Prosecutor's document, it is called M-83." Just as a clarification, I see here in this description of self-propelled hand-grenade the following sentence: "Like the MTHSD M-83, it was also marked as school rifle grenade ..." I would like to ask the witness: Is this, what we can see on the ELMO, a hand-grenade M-83 or a different one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All training equipment is marked in yellow, and they are used exclusively for training. But the shape is identical to combat equipment, so non-training equipment, in other words.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What we can see on the photograph on the ELMO, is that an M-83 used for training?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. However, their appearance is identical. Only this yellow stripe and yellow letter -- letters tell us that this is a school rifle grenade.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for that clarification. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. For the transcript, we have to say, I may have made a mistake. Under 2, it says: "Chemical rifle grenade SKE M-83." This is in the document provided to us by the Prosecutor. You see the document in front of you; right?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, chemical rifle grenade SKE M-83.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And the model of the grenade is M-79.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can we explain, for the benefit of the Trial Chamber, the significance of those numbers, M-79 and M-83? Could you please explain to the Trial Chamber and to us, if you know? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, "M" here refers to the 83 model or the year 1983 make, and the "79" means that the grenade was produced in the year 1979.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell the Trial Chamber whether you know if such chemical weapons or this particular chemical weapon was used in troops training? Is it still used by all the militaries and police forces in the world? And was it also used in all our police forces in the former Yugoslavia until 1995?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honour, the programme of training also encompasses a topic on the use of protection means, such as protective mask. And such a protective mask was applied and then troops would go through a chamber filled with tear gas for the training purpose.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is the purpose of those chemical weapons, used by all police forces in the world and previously used in the former Yugoslavia by the police and by the army, is their purpose to apply force against a certain person to render him incapable of performing a certain activity?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Tear gas was used as a means of riot control, forcing certain groups who barricaded themselves in a place to leave that place. And the effect of this tear gas is only temporary; it is not lethal.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Yesterday you were asked whether it is more humane to use this weapon, as a non-lethal agent, or would it be more humane to use a lethal weapon instead of a non-lethal weapon? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course it is more humane to use a non-lethal weapon.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please switch on the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise, Mr. President. Could this document please be tendered into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D201, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, since you told us yesterday that you had never spoken about the regress [as interpreted], that you didn't approve it, that you did not react to it, is it perhaps because that weapon is not a combat weapon and that it was not at the disposal of the Main Staff for combat? It was only part of the training equipment of the protective regiment. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sorry, but the translation doesn't make sense in English. I don't know what a regress is or how I see it, and so I don't know -- we're not going to know what the answer means. We should try it again maybe more slowly. They might catch it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The beginning of your question, Mr. Tolimir, is recorded in the following way: "Mr. Obradovic, since you told us yesterday that you had never spoken about the regress ..." Would you please repeat this first part of your question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The word used was "request."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The interpreters helped us. You were talking about request. Now it's --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Obviously it was a translation mistake.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question started like this: Yesterday you were asked and then you answered that you never considered this document. And then my question was this: Was it because of the fact that this equipment was training equipment for the military police and that the document basically referred to the military police?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you're talking about this document, we could not review this document or consider it because we never received it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now display 65 ter 7298. Can we see it again on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It is on the screen. If you press the --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, as you can see, the document never reached you, as you have told us. What we see there is "PkPO." What does that mean?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That means the assistant commander for logistics.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you please read the sentence under number 3, where the types of rifle grenades are listed. What does it say? Okay, I'll read it: "The 27th Logistics Base shall transport the aforementioned means to the command post of the 2nd Battalion of the 65th Protective Motorised Regiment and hand it over to the authorised representative of the 65th Protective Regiment." Thank you. My question is this: Does this mean that the means were sent exclusively to those to whom they were intended, pursuant to the rules of the former Yugoslavia? In this case, it would be the military police for the purposes that you have explained to us.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Microphone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Obradovic. We have now completed the group of questions about the use of training non-combat weapons. Thank you. And now we will take questions one at a time. But before that, let me ask you this: When we're talking about the enemy forces in the territory of the Federation of Bosnia-Herzegovina and the Republic of Croatia, which waged war against us, did they also use the same weapons for their regular activities?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Judge Mindua has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Witness. You recall that I put a question to you yesterday regarding P488. It's an exhibit that's signed by General Tolimir regarding his "chemical weapons," and regarding another document signed by the Lieutenant-Colonel Miroslav Cvijetic. So the letter signed by Lieutenant-Colonel Miroslav Cvijetic is now on the screen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm sorry. We have now the other document signed by General Tolimir on the screen. Shall we go back to the other one?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, not necessarily.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [Previous translation continues]... the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Thank you very much, Witness. So yesterday you said that it was possible that the letter from General Tolimir, from 21 July 1995, which bears the number P488, was a way to decoy or was a decoy to deceive the enemy. Now, after what you told us this morning, I would like to know if you still stand by what you said, or do you have some doubts this morning about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't have doubts. I told the Prosecutor that in my previous testimony I was unable to explain this and that this was illogical to me and that then subsequently, while I was here and when I read the Directive 7.1, I found that there could be some logic in the security support in the Directive 7.1, because we in the Staff did not discuss this memo that is addressed personally to General Miletic. I'm referring to the memo that we now see on the screens.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, I'm not really sure I understood your question [as interpreted]. As a matter of fact, I'm not quite sure you answered my question. You seemed to say yesterday that the letter of 21 July 1995 from -- written by General Tolimir could have been addressed or sent, or drafted, rather, to scare the enemy, to deceive the enemy as to the proposal of the use of chemical weapons or chemical means, so I would just like to know if you still maintain that this morning. Is this still a possibility, to your mind?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I did not claim, not even yesterday. I simply made a parallel with my answer that I gave to the Prosecutor in another case. I merely allowed for this possibility. Here, we should make a distinction between chemical assets and poisons, because chemical assets I used in various situation, including peace situation, while poisons are simply used in war. Of course, poisons also come within the domain of chemistry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MINDUA
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. President, it's the position of the Prosecution that this is the situation where the law - I believe it's Rule 90, though I'm not sure - is that the party putting questions is obligated to put his case to the witness so that it's clear to all of us is the position that -- in this case, is this document a decoy or is this a document -- a real document, and that the chemical weapons are as pointed out in the books and that's what it's talking about. That's what this law is designed to do so that we don't have the confusion that we have. So it's the obligation, in the Prosecution's view, that the Defence should put their case so that it's clear. Is this document a real document that's talking about these sorts of chemical weapons or is it a mine -- or is it, excuse me, a decoy? And I believe that's what that Rule is designed to help us with. I apologise for not having the number. It has to do with putting your case to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. It's 90(H)(ii).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: To make it clear for everybody in the courtroom, Rule 90(H)(i) reads as follows: "Cross-examination shall be limited to the subject-matter of the evidence-in-chief and matters affecting the credibility of the witness and, where the witness is able to give evidence relevant for the case for the cross-examining party, to the subject-matter of that case." And the next paragraph: "In the cross-examination of a witness who is able to give evidence relevant to the case for the cross-examining party, counsel shall put to that witness the nature of the case of the party for whom that counsel appears, which is in contradiction of the evidence given by the witness." This is the Rule Mr. McCloskey is referring to. Taking into account this Rule, Mr. Tolimir, could you explain what is your position on that and what are you putting to the witness in relation to this document?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. My questions pertain to chemical assets, and Mr. McCloskey now spoke about weapons, and there is a big distinction between combat assets and chemical assets. I never spoke about chemical weapons. I spoke about chemical assets. Let us take a look at the document on the screen. Paragraph 4, the second paragraph, where it says it would be best if we could achieve the destruction by use of chemical assets. I always speak about assets. I never speak about weapons. Can we now have -- and as for the parallel with the previous testimony of this witness in another case, I didn't make any parallel. I know nothing about it. Can we now have 2798 [as interpreted], the 65 ter number. That's a Prosecution document. Thank you. Okay, now we have it. It's 65 ter 7298. Thank you, I apologise. 7298, and it is P2155.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let us take a look at item 1, where it says: "The Command of the 27th Pob," Logistics Brigade, "shall, for the needs of the Drina Corps, transport the following items:" My question is: In this document, do they speak about weapons or assets? In the previous document, did I speak about chemical weapons or chemical assets? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: General Tolimir, a minor correction. It's not the 27th Brigade, it's Logistics Base, and they are to transport the assets, and not weapons.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Mr. President, I consistently spoke about assets. The witness consistently spoke about assets. We never spoke about weapons. If Mr. McCloskey wants to examine, in his re-examination, about weapons, he may do so, but I spoke about assets and both these documents spoke about assets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I would now like to see P122. Thank you. Can we have that in e-court. And before that, I have only one more question related to the previous subject-matter because of what the Prosecutor said.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is it possible to consider the use of those chemical assets they use in order to frighten the enemy and create certain propaganda effect?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible to view it like that, because the other side would not know what exactly you mean when you say "chemical assets."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This brings up the 90(H)(ii) situation. Is his position in cross-examination, as required, that this document is genuine and it's a proposal as stated, or is it a document merely to be a decoy, to be transmitted out? It's his -- he's -- it's incumbent upon him to say that in cross-examination. Now, perhaps Mr. Gajic can provide us the position of the Defence, but that's what this Rule is about, not leave us guessing is this a decoy or not. I think they can suggest that they don't need to answer it that way, but that's what this law is trying to get is so that the cross-examiner let's the trier of fact and the other party know what he's getting at. It can't be one or the other under this law. So right now it's -- is it either a document that's meant for a decoy and not real use or is it a real proposal to drop chemical assets on the enemy? That's what this law requires the Defence to tell us. Now, perhaps in this case Mr. Gajic could tell us.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I don't think that this could be the role of Mr. Gajic. That should be the role of Mr. Tolimir himself. But, Mr. McCloskey, if you look at the question Mr. Tolimir was putting to the witness on page 19, lines 21 through 23, he's not asking if the document is a decoy. He is, instead of that, asking, Is it possible to consider the use of those chemical assets, the use in order to frighten the enemy, and so on. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I -- that's exactly the way I took it as well, Mr. President, but it also -- it gets closer to the decoy issue. So it -- I thought at first, no, he's gotten away from the decoy issue; now he's talking in a kind of a hybrid situation. So I am still left, -- I don't know what the position of the Defence is on this point, and I think this Rule is designed to make it clear so that we all know what their position is. That's a duty that is placed on the Defence in cross-examination. It's one of the few duties that the Defence has, under the law, has to clear up, in my view.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Not only the Defence, but every cross-examining party if it's the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Especially the Prosecution in cross-examination, absolutely.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, what is your position?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. My position is: All this that Mr. McCloskey says, and if he doesn't have anything else to charge me, okay, I'll accept everything. I'm going to ask the witness to say something, and then you can judge for yourself whether it was a suggestive question or not, leading question or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us, when --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, it was not a question of leading questions. But is it your position that the document is a decoy to mislead the enemy? That was the question of Mr. McCloskey. Are you in the position to clarify that? You may need the assistance of Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I don't need the assistance of Mr. Gajic. I'm going to clarify this through my questions. There is no other way to do it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is: When chemical assets are used in stadiums and demonstrations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please wait a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber has considered the situation. We recall that the question of decoy and propaganda in misleading the enemy came up during the examination-in-chief by answers of the witness and not by questions of Mr. Tolimir. He commenced his cross-examination this morning, and I was referring to the clear language of the question we are talking about. At the moment, we don't see any need to put the Defence case to the Chamber and the witness by asking these questions. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you to the members of the Chamber. I already managed to put forward a part of my question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So, once again: Mr. Obradovic, when those chemical assets are used in stadiums, demonstrations, and riots, isn't the message then sent only to those who are directly affected by the use of those assets or to everybody else present at the stadium or in the demonstrations or in the riots? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, if you are talking about the direct --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I have to stop every speaker. We now receive French translation in the English channel, and the answer of the witness was not fully translated or not given; I have no idea. The answer starts with the words: "Well, if you are talking about the direct --" And then it stops. Please repeat your answer, and I hope that now we can receive it now in English.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. If you are referring to the direct effect to the people in the immediate vicinity, that's one thing. However, those people who are watching that what is happening from a distance, they also get the message.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Obradovic. I have no more questions related to this topic, the topic of the so-called chemical assets. Can we now have P122. I already requested it earlier, P122.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's on the screen, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: So now we can see the document. It was written on the 29th of July. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Does the first sentence say: "On the 28th of July, 1995, the Muslim side, on several occasions through UNPROFOR, asked for cessation of combat activities of the VRS in Zepa"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: "... saying that they are going to accept all terms of the agreement signed on the 24th of July." My question is: Do you know that an agreement was signed on the 24th which stipulated the surrender of all the weapons and then they refused it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was aware of that agreement but not of its contents.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now we can show the agreement, itself, so we can see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you maybe happen to know that Mr. Rupert Smith, in these proceedings, gave a statement about those events, and he said that he had information that negotiations with Slobodan Milosevic were underway so that the Muslim armed forces could cross the Drina River into Serbia? That's what he told us here three days ago. Do you maybe know about it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My Legal Assistant is now going to give us the exact reference, the date, and the page of the transcript. Thank you. I apologise. Now I found it. It was in P602. Because in line 12 to 7 during the cross-examination, Mr. Rupert Smith said the following, I quote: "I know that Carl Bildt led the negotiations, and I knew that at the time." Now he's talking about the time that he was in Zepa: "I knew that he achieved something and that it was possible for those people to cross the Drina River. Now, how that was done and who informed whom about what, I don't know exactly. I was told that this was classified information, that the negotiations were underway, and I did not know anything else about it at the time." Thank you. I still have to say one thing. General Smith spoke about it when he was asked about the situation in Zepa while he was in Zepa on the 26th and the 27th. So if he was then aware of the fact that the parties were negotiating, is it then justified to think that the Muslims could maybe cheat on that agreement and that they are not going to observe it? So when Tolimir points out the possibility of cheating, is it something realistic? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, only I didn't know what made you arrive at these conclusions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll read out to you the second paragraph of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You made a reference on page 24 to a document P602. I think that must be a mistake. And cross-examination of the witness Rupert Smith in lines 12 to 7, that can't be right either. If you are reading from a document, you should give a correct reference.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise for this wrong start. The transcript page is 11602. 11602, lines 12 through 17. I misread it, and that's why you got the wrong reference. Anyway, the right reference is 11602, pages [as interpreted] 12 through 17, and it's the transcript of the 22nd of March. Thank you. If I may, I would like to ask the witness a question now. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please take a look at the second paragraph on the following page in English: "In order to avoid being cheated by the Muslims, the implementation of the cessation of fire was conditioned by the liberation of all VRS members captured at Majevica, Lisaca, an Vijenac, in return for the liberation of the same -- the release of the same number of Muslims from the Batkovici Camp ..." et cetera. This document was written on the 28th, as we can see in the letterhead, and it mentions cheating as a possibility. Is it possible that the officer on the ground who knows the situation informs the superior command, stating his opinion and his assessment of the situation? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's why he is there in the first place.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm waiting for the recording of the answer of the witness. Thank you. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We heard that the general said that the document was dated the 28th. The document is, of course, dated the 29th. So I just -- that is an important document, so I just thought the record should -- we should catch that now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. McCloskey, for assisting. I'm glad you made it clear that it was the 29th, the last day of combat activities and the day when they crossed the Drina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please tell us, since it is said in this document, and Judge Mindua also asked you about it yesterday, that I said that the prisoners should not be registered until the cessation of combat activities -- take a look, please, we can see it here, where I say: "The persons you take prisoner until the cessation of fire shall not be registered or their name made public to the international organisations. We will keep them for the case if the Muslims do not carry out -- do not honour the agreement or manage to break out of the encirclement." Does this one day of non-disclosure until the cessation of fire -- is this a long time-period, when it comes to registering them with the International Red Cross? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that's not a long time-period, considering the conditions under which we worked and waged war.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, from your practice, is it usual to register prisoners during combat activities as soon as they are taken prisoner or only when there is a cessation of fire?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prisoners are taken at different locations. Sometimes it's one prisoner or two or three, but they are taken to a collection point outside of or away from combat activities.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. What is the purpose of this non-registering? Is it waiting for the combat to cease or is the purpose keeping them unregistered permanently?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The limiting factor here is the cessation of fire. It limits the time-period of non-registration.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let us take a look at document P1434. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: While we're waiting -- oh, here it is. It's a document of the command of the 1st Podrinje Light Infantry Brigade. It's their Security and Intelligence Organ, and it was drafted on 30 July. And my report was dated 29 July, so this is only one day later. And what does it say: "Since 28 July, 1995, the following Muslims have had the status of prisoners of war placed in the military holding centre in Rogatica." And this is followed by a list of Muslims with the status of prisoners of war.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please go until the end of the list, that is, item 45. That is the 45th prisoner of war registered with the Rogatica Brigade. So we're here at the end of the list, and we see that all of them are listed here, including the paragraph at the bottom of page 2. Could we please see it. Could we please see paragraph 2 in e-court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Page 2, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see item C, "Treatment." It's on the following page in English. I quote from the first paragraph here: "In keeping with the orders of General Tolimir and his instructions, we have taken all necessary measures, and as far as possible --" I can't see this well.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Mainly."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: " ... mainly honoured. Among others, the following was done." And then it goes on to speak about the categories of prisoners. And then we see the sixth bullet point, or the seventh, actually: "The healthy are in one room, the wounded and sick in another room, and the members of the former leadership are in a third room." And then the following bullet point: "Atlantida is separated and is placed at another location that has better accommodation." The person in question is Avdo Palic. The following bullet point says: "The effendi is allowed to pray in a room five times a day." Now, tell us, please, can we see from this document that all prisoners of war who were available at the time, pursuant to my orders, were registered with the Red Cross? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, General Tolimir just said that the person called Atlantida is Avdo Palic, and I would like to agree with the Defence on that fact so we can get an agreed fact on the record. As we know, statements that the Defence say are not facts and not part of the record, but it appears that he is offering that as a fact, and so I would accept his offer and agree with him. It's an awkward situation, I understand, but I am sure he'll agree with me on that. But then it would at least give you the ability to hold that as a fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, this, I take it, as an invitation to the Defence to negotiate on that fact?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, it is, basically, yes, because I'm -- I think he said this a couple of times, so I'm pretty sure that's what he wants you to know. And, of course, under our situation, for you to be able to count on that, we need an agreement, as far as I'm reading and understanding how we've -- how you have set up his questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, the parties should come in contact and discuss this topic. But now we are in cross-examination of the witness, and the last question was: "Sir, can we see --" and I quote: "Can we see from this document that all prisoners of war who were available at the time, pursuant to my orders, were registered with the Red Cross?" That was the question. Could you please answer that.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is what this document speaks about.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I must say that I actually said, According to the assertions of the OTP, the person called Atlantida is Avdo Palic. This wasn't my assertion. And then this also mentions an effendi who is allowed to pray. Let us clarify.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, may I interrupt you. Just for the record, I see on the record, page 29, lines 16 to 18, I quote: "... and then the following bullet point: "'Atlantida is separated and is placed at another location and is a better accommodation.' "The person in question is Avdo Palic." "Avdo" is not included yet in the record. But you were not referring to the Prosecution's position. You said that. This is what we have heard and what we have on the record.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: The interpreter may have misheard what the general said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That may be checked on the tape. Please continue. We don't need any discussion. I just wanted to clarify the record. But we have now received the notice of the interpreters. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: The second bullet point below "Atlantida" says: "The effendi is allowed to pray in the room five times a day." Here's my question: Did you know that there was an effendi in Zepa and that he was taken prisoner? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: An effendi is a priest. I suppose that there would be one, because Zepa is a populated place with a house of worship. But I didn't know that he was taken prisoner.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat his question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, you started with your question while the interpretation was going on. Please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you know that in Zepa there was an effendi who was a priest and another effendi who was not and he was the president of the War Presidency of Zepa? His name was Hajrudin.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Actually, his name was Hajric, not Hajrudin. Let's see what a member of the War Presidency said about that on the 13th of August, 2010. On transcript page 4543, lines 14 through 22, here's what he says, this other member of the War Presidency: "As far as I know --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the page number. It was not recorded.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The 30th of August, 2010, transcript page 4543, lines 14 through 22. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here is what this witness said, I quote: "As far as I know, Mr. Hajric was not a religious minister in Zepa. He was a hodja, but he was not a religious leader. Before the war, he worked in another village. In Zepa, there was a hodja, and he was there during the war and performed these duties. As far as I know, he was a hodja in Pozeplje," he, referring to Hajric, the one taken prisoner, "and when the war broke out, he came to Zepa. At any rate, he didn't work as the hodja of Zepa because during the war another person did that job and that was the same person who had been there earlier. Hajric simply at that time did not go about that job." Then the question was: "Was he president of the War Presidency? Did he work as a hodja?" On page 4544, lines 2 through 3, he replies: "No, never. That was his capacity when he worked as hodja in another place in 1992." Now we will show you the agreement that you wanted to see. We will show it in e-court. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the Court please produce -- thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was the hodja treated fairly? Was he allowed to exercise his religious rights and freedoms, the one who was taken prisoner? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that the treatment was fair. The Islamic faith orders its followers to pray five times a day, and here we see that he was, indeed, allowed to pray five times a day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the accused, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Your microphone, your microphone. You need your microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Thank you, Mr. President. I apologise to the Trial Chamber and to you, because at the moment I don't have the agreement on me. I thought I did, but I don't. I promised that I would show it to you. Its number is D51, my Legal Adviser tells me. Could the Court please produce D51, and then you will be able to see it on the screen. We will not dwell upon it too long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have it on the screen now.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: You see we have this agreement, and it says in its first paragraph: "Agreement on the disarmament of the able-bodied population in the Zepa enclave." And then paragraph 1, line 1, it says: "On 24th of July, 1995, the following agreement was reached between Rajko Kusic, on the one side, and Hamdija Torlak, on the other, in the presence of UNPROFOR representative Sejmon Dudnjik." And then the document proceeds to describe the agreement, where it says that: "All Muslims will hand in their weapons." Under bullet point 2, we can see that: "Avdo Palic shall issue an order to his troops to withdraw from the defence line and refugee groups together with the population, and from the centre of settlements and villages, and not to try to cross illegally through the territory of Republika Srpska." Thank you. My question is this: Does the document have or could it form the basis for an estimate that the Muslims dragged their feet when it came to this surrender, since they avoided to sign the document -- the agreement from the 24th to the 29th, when I issued that document that we saw previously on the screen? Thank you. This is document P122, in which I spoke about possible deceptions on the part of the Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I have to stop you. This is a very confusing way to put questions to the witness. You have put a question to him and didn't wait for his answer, and now you're going on and on. You have quoted from different documents in the transcript. Please let the witness answer. Sir, do you recall the last question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My answer to the previous question would be, Yes, the person who was appraised of the agreement and who was on the ground can draw a conclusion on what was happening on the ground and the aberrations in the conduct of the people from what was achieved by the agreement that had been reached.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: -- it is the time for our first break. It's not helpful to read too many documents into the record. Thank you very much. We adjourn and resume at 11.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber would like to raise the problem of today's hearing and today's session and if it is likely or not likely that we will finish with the witness today. The Chamber would like to make very clear for you, Mr. Tolimir, that you are not at all under a time pressure. You requested six hours. You will have the six hours. You will have even more, since the Prosecution has used more. To make that very clear. If you think you will be able to finish today, that's fine, but the Prosecution needs time for re-examination, I suppose. And, therefore, both parties should consider if it's really a good idea to have this extended sitting today if the witness has to come back at a later stage anyway. You should think about that during the second session and we should agree at the end of the second session on that. But, now, please continue your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'll try and finish as you have instructed me. I'm going to follow the same schedule of questions that the Prosecution has used so they will not need to re-examine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: On the 29th of March, on transcript page 11928, the Prosecution asked you whether the 327th Brigade has become part of the VRS after the abolishment of the 11th Corps of the JNA. You said "Yes." And then on line 10, you were asked whether that brigade became part of VRS. Again the question was asked and again you say "Yes." Bearing in mind the reference, page numbers, my question is this: Did Muslim and Croat officers leave your brigade after their respective republics had been recognised by the European Union and NATO as independent states, and did only Serbs remain in your brigade? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that I stated in one part of my answer that when the Slovenians left for Slovenia and the Croats for Croatia, the Muslim members joined the BiH army. And when the officers from Serbia went back to Serbia and Montenegro, people who remained were not all Serbs, but, in any event, they were members of the Serbian people, and only a few of them represented some other ethnic groups for their own interest.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us the dates or periods whenever you answer a question because this is very important for the record. I would like to repeat just one part of my question. I would like to rephrase it as well. When did Slovenians return to Slovenia, when did Croats return to Croatia, when did Serbs return to Serbia, and when did Muslims from Bosnia and Herzegovina leave the JNA units in Bosnia and Herzegovina? Could you please give us a time-frame for all of that.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some left even before the recognition of particular republics of the former state. And those who went back to Serbia and Montenegro did that after the decision on the withdrawal was reached on the 19th of May, I believe. And when the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina was recognised - the process was completed on the 6th of April - that's when the whole process ended, in terms of people going back to their respective republics.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber who recognised the secession of Slovenia, Croatia, and Bosnia? You used the term "after the recognition." Who was it who recognised those republics, which international body? Was that the Security Council, the European Union, NATO? Who was it who recognised those states?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First, there were some individual states who did that. And when it came to Bosnia and Herzegovina, I believe that the Federal Republic of Germany was among the first who recognised it. And then there was the Holy See. And later on the Security Council also recognised those republics.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us whether after the war in Slovenia, and you will tell us when that happened, whether the secession of Slovenia followed the war in Slovenia and whether any of the European states recognised Slovenia as an independent state? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The Republic of Slovenia was the first republic to secede from the former state. I don't know exactly whether that was in 1991. After a very short war, Austria and Germany were among the first states that recognised Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you remember, as a member of the army and the brigade commander, whether Croatia remained an integral part of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia after the secession of Slovenia?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, in formal and legal terms it was still an integral part of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you perhaps know whether the republics could secede from the federal state of Yugoslavia of their own will, without a prior consent of all the other republics that constituted the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and do you perhaps know how the Constitution of the federative state of Yugoslavia envisaged such a situation?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the Constitution, there was a term "unity until secession," but that was a condition that applied on people's or ethnic groups. When it came to the secession of particular republics, all the members of the federations had to agree to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, could you tell us whether the other members of the federation, Serbia, Macedonia, Croatia, and others, approved the secession of Yugoslavia [as interpreted] or not?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter's correction: The secession of Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you discharge the duties as a brigade commander in Derventa during the war in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you know what year was the war in Croatia taking place and who was the president of the federal government at the time?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The war in Croatia was in 1991, and in 1992 the president of the Presidency at the time was Jovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Was Stipe Mesic perhaps the president of the Presidency during the war in Croatia? When was Stipe Mesic the president of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. After Jovic, according to the principle of rotation, Stipe Mesic assumed those duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Isn't this a unique example in the world? A republic is trying to secede from the federal state and its member, presiders of the federal government? Wouldn't that be a precedent?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is nonsense because as a member of the Presidency he swore that he would serve the federal state and that he would fight for its sovereignty and integrity. On the other side, he does just the opposite and helps its break-up, and he helps the Republic of Croatia, which is trying to secede.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You have to stop yet again. You are overlapping again. The last question of you, Mr. Tolimir, was not interpreted and not recorded because the speaker was still -- the witness was still speaking and his answer was in translation. Please repeat your last answer, and be reminded -- your last question, and be reminded not to overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'll bear that in mind. I repeat my question.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you know what Mr. Stipe Mesic stated after he had left his position as the president of the Presidency of the SFRY and when the secession of Croatia from Yugoslavia was recognised? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know if I'm going to quote his words correctly. In any case: My mission is accomplished, Yugoslavia no longer exists.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Obradovic, do you remember, who was it who imposed and set conditions for him to be the president of Yugoslavia at the time when Croatia waged war against the rest of that same Yugoslavia and wanted to secede from it by force? Thank you. I apologise. Let me be precise. What international body was it that imposed Mr. Mesic as the president of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was the Security Council that insisted that the principle of rotation that had been in place should be honoured.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Are you perhaps sure that it was the Security Council, or maybe somebody else?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Let me correct myself. I stand corrected. It was the European Community. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Are these examples of the European Community interfering with the internal affairs of Yugoslavia, both the European Community and its [indiscernible] commission, that highlighted the formulae that you explained for us?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Judging by the course of events, my answer would be yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. My question is this: Do you know, before the 15th of May and before the establishment of the VRS, did Muslims and Croats leave your brigade and returned and joined their respective national armies?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some parties, namely the HDZ and the SDA, that were ethnic parties, exerted influence on the officers of the JNA, and they recruited them for their newly-established militaries, the Patriotic League and the National Defence or the Territorial Defence, respectively.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Obradovic. Do you perhaps know when is the day of the state of Bosnia and Herzegovina celebrated, when is the day of the Army of Bosnia and Herzegovina celebrated, and when the Patriotic League was established, in what month?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that it was the end of March or the beginning of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you please give us the year for the record? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell the Trial Chamber whether the rest of the men who were on the strength of your brigade joined the VRS, or were they forced to defend themselves from the newly-established military formations that threatened them? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was talking about the officers. However, the influence of national leaderships was exerted on everybody. The brigade bore the so-called R classification, which means that it was manned from the reserve forces.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Therefore, under the influence of those parties and leaderships, did not respond to mobilisation calls and failed to join their units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us whether anybody from the reserve strength of your brigade participated in the war in Croatia?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Nobody from my brigade participated in the war in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know whether any of the other JNA units deployed in Bosnia and Herzegovina were used in the war that was waged in Croatia against the JNA? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I know that some units from the 5th Corps of the former JNA, that's the corps that was stationed in Banja Luka, because a significant area from which they withdrew their manpower was in Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since your brigade was from the R classification, when the 17th Corps of the JNA was evacuated on the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina after the decision of the European Union and after the control of the cease-fire in Croatia, is it then logical that those soldiers who are reservists from those places should remain in the establishment of which they used to belong before that in their own place of residence and that they should be on the list of military conscripts in that place?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's what would normally happen. Yes, that's what happened. They mostly remained. And a certain number of officers also remained in that area. I also remained in that area because I hail from Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell the Trial Chamber, if you know, where was the headquarters of UNPROFOR during the war in Croatia that was observed by the EU observers who at the time wore white uniforms? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure. I think that their headquarters was in Zagreb. But also the representatives of European Community used to come in white uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you maybe remember whether the whole federation gave the assets from the former federal government and sent them to the headquarters in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't know about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you know that during the war in Croatia all the representatives of the international community left Sarajevo for Zagreb?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that point to a conclusion? How could a certain territory be safe for them until the end of the war in Croatia and then that territory was not safe for them when the war in Croatia ended? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you for that answer.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was probably the question of their own attitude and convictions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you for your answers. On which date did you join the establishment of the VRS together with the remaining manpower in the brigade? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was the 19th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did then the complete establishment of the 17th Corps, headed by General Jankovic, leave all the barracks and all the garrisons and crossed over to the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia because those people wanted to live in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Only those who chose to stay in Bosnia and Herzegovina did not leave.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please tell us whether the Army of Republika Srpska was formed independently after the 19th of May when Jankovic left with his corps and after the decision and the pressure exerted on the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia to promulgate such a decision, the decision to withdraw the republican organs belonging to other republics from the territory of Bosnia and Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Together with the remainder of those volunteers, in the given circumstances in the territory, I joined the 1st Krajina Corps, that is, the corps that was headquartered in Banja Luka. The former corps was headquartered in Tuzla; I mean the 17th Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since there was some confusion about whether European Union or United Nations took part in that process, can you tell us, would it be logical, would it be justified, for the Security Council to decide that a certain state should leave its sovereign territory, or was it decided by some other organs? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This was based on the general attitude of the European Union.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you were a member of the army before the outbreak of war in Bosnia and Herzegovina, tell us, was the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina incited from abroad? And after such incitement, such as the recognition, did the break-up of Yugoslavia ensue? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The act of recognition, itself, did stir up the conflict, in a way.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Looking at the situation from the aspect of the international law, is it lawful for certain countries to recognise the secession of certain parts of some other country before the Security Council does that same thing?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not lawful.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Obradovic. Let us now move on to the diagram that you were shown on page 24 of the transcript dated the 29th of March. It's 65 ter 7295. If you have the original diagram that you yourself drew, it would be good if you could keep it at hand so that we can compare it with the diagram that was shown to us by the Prosecution on the screens and that now bears a number 65 ter 7295. Thank you. We can now see it on the screen. It's 65 ter 7295. This is the diagram used by the Prosecution during the examination-in-chief. And if you have your original diagram at hand, could you please compare the two diagrams and tell us which elements from your diagram were not faithfully reproduced in this diagram?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't have my own diagram at hand. When we talk about the differences between what we see on the screens and what I drew, I can tell you that the differences pertain mostly to the lines of communications and command. In my diagram, at the same level, looking from left to right, will you find the sectors of the Main Staff, and then you can see the lines going towards the commander, because each sector has a connection with the commander.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can I ask the Usher to hand you the diagram that you drew by your own hand so that you don't have to speak without it. My Legal Assistant can hand you the diagram if the Prosecution does not have it at hand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, it should be forwarded to the witness. Mr. McCloskey, the Chamber has also two copies -- hard copies of that. I'm not sure if we have already admitted these two diagrams into evidence. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, yes. The purpose of my direct with that diagram was to allow the witness to correct it. And I do have our most latest corrections which I provided last night to the Defence so they could review it to see if they had any changes or concerns, so I wouldn't be asking the original that he helped us fix, but I do have another one. I was waiting to speak to Mr. Gajic before I offered it into evidence. And, of course, his original, no objection it going into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. First, I would like to take a look at the difference between this diagram, which was the basis for the examination-in-chief, and the original diagram drawn by the witness.
