And then later on we can also take a look at this new diagram that was mentioned just now in order to find out whether there are still some differences between that diagram and the original diagram.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us, what differences can you see between the diagram on the screen and the diagram drawn by you? Let's go from left to right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wrote and drew the first item on the left side, and that first item is "Staff Sector," and there is a connection between the Staff Sector and the commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And who was in that Staff Sector?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Lieutenant General Manojlo Milovanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And then ...?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And then at the same level, Sector for Moral Guidance, Religious and Legal Affairs, Lieutenant-Colonel General Milan Gvero. And then in the same level follows Sector for Logistics, headed by General Djukic. And then continuing in the same level, Sector for Organisation, Mobilisation and Personnel Affairs, Major General Skrbic. Following in the same level, Sector for Intelligence and Security Affairs, headed by Major General Zdravko Tolimir. And then in the same level, Autonomous Administrations, beginning with Administration for Planning, Development, and Finance, headed by General Tomic. And still in the same level, Administration for Air Force and Air Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you indicate ranks for all the officers who were commanders or chiefs?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, at the beginning I did indicate it for you and some other generals. And then after the intervention from Judge Mindua, I gave precise information about the rank of each person because colonel-general is a higher rank than lieutenant-general and major-general.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let us now take a look again at the diagram. Can we see that every officer has his rank and function mentioned here?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, this is in English, so I wouldn't know about the ranks. Also, the sequence is not the same. I insisted on this. And I gave the sequence of sectors according to the establishment book because it also shows a sort of hierarchy. First you have Staff Sector, which is headed by the person performing the duty of the deputy commander, and then they are ranked sequentially. And at the bottom we find administrations, which are of lower ranking but they are autonomous.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We are going to see more about this hierarchy in 65 ter 3903, which is the rule book. However, what you just said is sufficient for me. I also know that Mr. McCloskey told us that he prepared a new diagram, so now we can also check whether this new diagram corresponds to your handwritten diagram. And if not, you should tell us what should be corrected. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is that new diagram, the corrected one, already in e-court?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, Mr. President. I was hoping to get the exchange of information before we put it in e-court so that we wouldn't be, hopefully, having too many drafts. But I don't think there's going to be any disagreement on this, the ranks or the hierarchy. It's all very well established. We had some issues, understanding his Cyrillic, is why I had to do a bit of that in the court. So I don't think there's any problem here. We should work together to be able to get a good diagram reflecting the general's views on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We had this exercise of pointing out the actual ranks at the relevant time of the people in the diagram yesterday, and that was, indeed, a good clarification. Mr. Gajic, I saw you on your feet.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I have a copy that I received from the Prosecution. Apart from the ranks, there are some small differences compared to the copy that is currently in e-court. I think, nevertheless, that this diagram drawn up by the Prosecution should be given to the witness for him to take a look.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, please. If there are more copies available, the Chamber would like to receive some as well. I see the Prosecution has given one copy to the witness directly. If the Chamber -- Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We have them for the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would be grateful for a copy for myself, if there is one. If not, I'll rely on my memory.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now you have one. Please continue, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Considering the time and your wish to travel back, I will not -- I'll try not to waste much time. Take a look at this schematic and see if it matches your original. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The sequence in which the sectors are depicted does not match my original. I said that it was important to honour the sequence as laid out in the establishment book. It starts with the Staff Sector and goes on with some other sectors in the relevant sequence. That is the difference, and I consider it important because that's how it is laid out in the establishment book.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Obradovic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Talking about this, could we please see 65 ter 0393. That's the rule book about the powers of the staffs and corps commands in peacetime. The sequence is also dealt with there. The page reference -- well, we see the cover page now in both languages. Then there is page 2. Could we please see page 3 in Serbian, which is page 2 in English. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here on this page, page 2, we see that under the commander there are the other organs in the very sequence that you have explained. And under 2.4, we see it says "Organs for Branches." Yesterday this was a disputed issue. What can you tell us about this organ?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The combat arms organ was headed -- or each of these was headed by the representative of one of the combat arms of the army, starting from the infantry and then followed by the artillery, armoured and mechanised units, engineers units, communications, APC defence, and the artillery and rocket units of anti-aircraft defence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let us see page 17 in Serbian and page 14 in English, where this combat arms organ is dealt with. Let's see how it was translated. I see that the translation is correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And we see that it explains -- or, rather, do explain to us what this organ is for and what its remit includes.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's stated right at the beginning. It says: "Organs for Branches are specialist organs of the staff responsible for the combat readiness of corps branch units, and in this regard, they shall:"

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us what these combat arms so, or, rather, their chiefs, that is, the officers serving in these combat arms.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They keep an operative register of these combat arms units. This has to do with both the personnel and the armaments, and they are in charge of building the combat readiness of these units. Based on these registers, they can make proposals to the Chief of Staff about the use of any such unit at any given time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since they submit proposals for use, do they have the right to command these units in accordance with their proposals? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They do not have the right to command these units, and that is why I insisted on this in my schematic and depicted the lines of subordination between the commander and the individual units. And I forgot to enter one unit which is -- which is a unit catering for the needs of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you're a highly-trained officer, which we know from your CV, can you tell us who it is, then, who commands the units?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And possibly we can look at Article 6 on page 5, which is the third page in English and the fourth page in Serbian. Thank you. Actually, it's page 4 in English and page 5 in Serbian. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We see Article 6 here, and it reads: "The right to command units and institutions of the organic compound of KoV/Land Army Corps, is under the exclusive responsibility of the commander. Units and institutions outside the corps' organic compound, those temporarily subordinated, are commanded and controlled by the commander only within the limits of the stipulated authorities' powers." Please explain this to the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is clear that the commander has the exclusive right to command units. At certain points in time it is possible to re-subordinate a unit that belongs -- that organically belongs to another unit. It can be re-subordinated to the corps and then the corps commander - and the corps has been reinforced with that unit - gets the right to command that unit in a certain area and during a certain time-period, but he cannot go beyond that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let us now take a look at page 7 in Serbian and page 6 in English, where the powers of the commander are explicitly stated.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I will read it out first and then ask my question. I quote: "The commander shall command and control subordinate units and institutions within the scope of the responsibility received," or authority received. "He shall be responsible to his superior for his work and the situation in subordinate units and institutions and for proper and timely execution of work and tasks in the competence of the command organ." You, as an officer who commanded a brigade and who was in a high position at corps level and also in the Main Staff, please interpret this provision for us, and how does it apply to the commander with regard to his subordinates and institutions?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is based on the singleness of command. The commander has the exclusive right to command, and he is responsible for the overall level of combat readiness. And for that, he is responsible to his superior; he, and nobody else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let us now look at page 7 in Serbian and 8 in English. We're interested in paragraph 6, which is about controlling the security organ. This is item 6 of Article 9.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you please explain to us the difference between the B/C/S term "rukovodjenje" and "control" in English?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The B/C/S term is "rukovodjenje i komandorvanje," which is translated into English as "command and control." Institutions are controlled, whereas units are commanded.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I will read it out. It says: "Controls the security service," the commander is meant, "and is responsible for the security support to the command and subordinate units and institutions and takes measures in line with the rules and his authority."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: If the general could direct all of us, and especially the interpreters, so when he is reading one of these important sections the interpreters are able to get the -- this is the CLSS, and there's a lot of work that's gone into this, and so now we're -- the words are, of course, changing because of the nature of the languages, of course. But if he can direct them so that the interpreters can see that, then the record will be consistent with the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. Tolimir did that. On line 15, page 54, he said : "This is item 6 of Article 9." And he was reading the item 6. But I think at this point in time the interpreters didn't get the same wording as we can see in the translation on the screen. But I think this is now clear on the record, what --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. It's very difficult, obviously.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, we have slight problems with the translations of some terms. That's why Mr. Tolimir is trying to explain the meaning of some of them with the witness. I hope that we will be able to agree with the Prosecution on some translations. Unfortunately, we are not always in the position to scrutinize all translations.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This will be an ongoing problem in all trials in this Tribunal. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, we will work together with him. However, the definition of "command" is something that is so fundamental to this case that we will -- we should get together immediately on this so that there's no disagreement on that crucial point. This isn't just a document that we're trying to figure out. This has been fundamental and been part of this institution for many years.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise, but the problem here is not with the word "command" or "commanding." The problem is the B/C/S term "rukovodjenje" or, in English, "directing," whereas it's being interpreted as "control" or "controlling."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed that might be the problem. Mr. Tolimir, please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, since you were commander at your time and you both commanded and controlled, please tell the Trial Chamber what "command" is and what "control" is, because you said that units are commanded and institutions are controlled.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please continue. Please continue with your answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that yesterday or the day before yesterday I said that commanding or command has five functions according to the theory according to which the JNA worked and later the VRS. The first function of command is planning; that accounts for 25 per cent. Secondly, there's organisation; it accounts for 50 per cent. Third is issuing orders, which accounts for 10 per cent. Fourth is co-ordination, which accounts for 10 per cent. And fifth is "kontrola," which accounts for 5 per cent of the total. In principle, units are commanded; whereas institutions are controlled, which in B/C/S it's -- the verb is "rukovoditi."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please provide me of an example of an institution existing at that time which would relate to this comment you gave us? What is an institution?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, the training centre is not a unit; it's a training institution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, since there are different translations, the B/C/S terms "rukovodjenje," "kontrola," and "komandorvanje," under item 6 we see that it says, in B/C/S, "rukovodi." Does that mean that such services as the Security Service or support arm are actually -- actually fall under the term "rukovodjenje," "control"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness please repeat his answer.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now we have really trouble. If you look at the transcript, you can see the interpreters didn't catch everything and they asked you to repeat the answer. We are dealing with specific terms and their meaning, and now we are slightly confused, if you look at the transcript. Could you please repeat your answer very slowly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I mentioned one institution, the Military Schools Centre, but the sectors are not units at the level of command. So within the command, there is control, but units are commanded. And clearly the commander implements command through lower-level commands, whereas planning, organisation, issuing orders, and what is called "kontrola," in B/C/S, is carried out through his command organs in the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Perhaps I can just identify the problem, which has always been a problem. It's a language problem. The terms "rukovodjenje" and the verb that the translator gave us and the term "kontrola" both get translated in English as "control," but they're essentially two different concepts in the -- in the JNA and VRS. So that's where we have problems, and that's why the translation issues are so difficult.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, unfortunately I know that probably other participants in this proceeding are confused. I'm the only one here who speaks both Serbian and English. I think that the translation of "rukovodjenje" should be "directing" or "direction." And as for "control," it's "kontrola." The word is almost the same in Serbian and English. You can find it under the quotation mark here. I think that this Defence is going to spend lots of time merely to request the verification of this transcript, but this is something that we are definitely going to have to do, and it's really going to take lots of time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm not convinced that it is necessary to dwell on this any further. We have all the problems now on the transcript, we have the comments, the different definitions, and at a later point in time we should try to get an authorised translation. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: On that point, Mr. President, this concern was litigated in the Popovic case. These materials were given to CLSS and they came through with their final version on this after their experience and study. So we have been through this before. And we will connect with Mr. Gajic and CLSS to try to have him see that, but I don't believe there's any reason to go through this all over again. It's the identical issue. CLSS has dealt with it. It should be reflected in these documents. Now, if he comes up with documents that are a little different, we may have to revisit it, but this is a fundamental core document that has been dealt with, that was dealt with by CLSS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Not to waste more time, we should continue. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I would like the witness to state whether practical actions of "rukovodjenje" and "komanda" and "kontrola" are three different things, in practice.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you explain the difference between "rukovodjenje" and "kontrola"? Because this seems to be in dispute.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Kontrola" is performed by the commander by way of his immediate insight or through his organs. It is performed in a certain space, in a certain time, in a certain unit. "Rukovoditi" means to direct or manage a certain institution or part of the command in its realisation of the task assigned. And a part of "komandovanje," "command," is "kontrola."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Obradovic. And now we are going to obey the advice of the Presiding Judge and move on to another topic. Can you take a look at page 19 in Serbian, page 16 in English. I would like to take a look at 2.6, "Organ for Intelligence Work"; more specifically, Article 17. Now you have it in front of you. Since there are some translations in circulation where those three words are used interchangeably, I would like us now to take a look at the exact competence of the Organ for Intelligence Work. I quote Article 17: "The Organ for Intelligence and Reconnaissance Work is responsible for: "Planning, organising, and directing intelligence and reconnaissance activities in the corps' zone of responsibility." My question is: Based on item 1 in Article 17, can he command, does he have the right to command, or does he merely perform planning and organising?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Command is an exclusive jurisdiction of the commander. He can only plan and organise activities and also direct intelligence organs of the subordinate units in their activities in the field of gathering and processing of information, information pertaining to the enemy, to the combat zone, to the weather, to his own forces, and so on and so forth, in land and in the air, and elsewhere, depending on where they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just a moment. I would like to clarify something. You said, Witness: "Command is the exclusive jurisdiction of the commander." In itself that seems to be clear. But referring to this Sector for Intelligence, are you referring to the commander of the Main Staff or the assistant commander for security and intelligence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The commander discharges this duty through his assistant, who heads the Sector of Intelligence and Security Work, who then forwards this to the Intelligence and Security Administration, and down there to the units. So they plan and organise intelligence and security and reconnaissance activities. He directs the subordinate intelligence organs in the subordinate units and defines the core of their activity in information-gathering field.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. You said "he." To whom are you referring?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm referring to the intelligence organ at this level. Here, it happens to be the corps. If we talk about the Main Staff, then I'm referring to the chief of the Security Administration --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Intelligence Administration, interpreter's correction.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] -- because the chief of sector is going to delegate his authority to the chief of the administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I didn't quite understand. You said --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the Intelligence and Securities Sector is headed by Major General Tolimir. The segment pertaining to intelligence work within the sector falls within the purview of the chief of the Intelligence Administration, headed by Colonel Salapura.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And, again, you said "he" -- just a moment. "He can only plan and organise activities and also direct intelligence organs ..." You are referring to Mr. Salapura or General Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we are not talking about combat activity here; we are talking about intelligence-gathering activity. Commander, through General Tolimir, who is the chief of the sector, requests something that is Tolimir then going to forward to Colonel Salapura, and then he is going to plan the intelligence activity. That's his job. He heads that segment of the sector.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, since you told us that intelligence/security organs plan and organise, can you tell us explicitly, do they have the right to command any of the units within their establishment? If it's the corps, within the corps; if it's a brigade, within the brigade; if it's the staff, within the staff. Do they have the right to command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They do not have the power to command.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does that mean that they are only competent to plan, direct, and organise, and only the commander can command?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now take a look specifically at the work of the work of the intelligence organs. We now see that the Trial Chamber, itself, is interested in the work of intelligence organs. And now let us take a look at the security organs. It's item 7, page 35 in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not catch the page in English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we zoom in. It's Article 29 in Chapter 7. All right. You can see now Article 29.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, here we can see Article 29, which goes as follows: "The security organ is a specialised organ of the command for organising and implementing security measures and undertaking other specialised work in the field of security that are placed under its responsibility by special regulations and is in this regard responsible for:" Et cetera. So, since Article 29 forms the basis for all other items that follow here, from 1 to 14, could you tell us, is it possible for the security organ in any situation to command any establishment, even a small squad which is the smallest formational unit?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: He does not have that authority.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you explain the words "the security organ is a specialised organ"? What does it mean, "a specialised organ"?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Every level of command will have security, organ who is professionally trained to perform security work, and that is the meaning in which he plans and organises work of the subordinated security organs within that field.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. What's the difference between being professionally trained for one thing and being specialised for it?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, being professional is more general and being specialised is more narrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I apologise, but I have to ask you because in the transcript sometimes these two words appear as synonyms; they are translated by the same word. Here in item 1 we can see: "Uncovering and preventing intelligence and other subversive activities of foreign intelligence services and hostile Yugoslav emigrés aimed against the corps and the armed forces as a whole and their members for undertaking tasks in peacetime, emergency situations, during an imminent threat of war, and in wartime." My question is: When we talk about specialised/professional intelligence organs, are they responsible to the commander for all that is listed here, all those activities of uncovering subversive activities in peacetime and imminent threat of war? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they report to the commander for their activity of preventing such activities within the zone of responsibility of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Item 2 begins with "Uncovering," and that work is characteristic for the whole item too.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I have to stop you because the record stopped. I don't know what happened.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I see we only can follow the record on LiveNote. In e-court, it stopped on page 64, line 11. But we have it in LiveNote. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just -- I think it will save time. And the general said that this applied in the situation of the corps. Could we clarify if this would also be the same for the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: The duties that the security organ has in the corps, are they equivalent to their duties at the level of the Main Staff? In other words, does the security organ of the Main Staff have the right to command lower units?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It does not have the right to command. However, its activity is expanded to the general zone under the control of the VRS, while the corps organs are only responsible for the zone under the control of the corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We don't have much time, so let us take a look at item 1. It says: "Uncovering and preventing intelligence and subversive activities." Item 2: "Uncovering and preventing hostile activities ..." Item 3: "Undertaking counter-intelligence measures and activities ..." Item 4: "Participating in uncovering and preventing serious crimes ..." Item 5: "Performing security checks on persons ..." Item 6: "Participating in proposing, prescribing, and organising security and self-protection measures ..." Seven: "Participating in planning --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please slow down.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I shall repeat.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Six: "Participating --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just continue, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Seven: "Participating in planning and programming security training ..." And then: "Participating in making the utilisation plan ..." And so on and so forth. Let us stop here at item 8. Or maybe we can also go on over to number 9: "Expertly directing security organs ..." Ten: "Proposing officers for reinforcement of security organs ..." Eleven: "Completing security preparations of members of the corps ..." "Completing preparations for working conditions of emergency ..." Thirteen: "Performing jobs in the field of planning, development, and routine preparations ..." Fourteen: "Performing other work and tasks prescribed by the Rules of Service of Security Organs of the Armed Forces and other professional/specialised regulations." Now, bearing in mind those 14 items which define the work of the security organ in the corps, is there a single item bestowing the right to command, and does all this -- at the level of the corps, is this all equivalent to the level of the Main Staff, only the zone of responsibility is wider? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the tasks are identical, but the scope is different -- or, rather, the size of the territory is different and there's no command competence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now go to bullet point 5 of Article 29, or, rather, paragraph 5 in Chapter 7, the security organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: That paragraph reads: "Performing security checks on persons engaged for peacetime and wartime service in corps commands ..." My question is this: Yesterday, on the examination-in-chief, you were shown a document in which I say that the commander's order was not carried out and that the sabotage unit was not manned to the full capacity. Please, was that within my authority, to carry out the security check, and is that why I asked them why they did not recruit the necessary number of men? Thank you. Would that have anything to do with my authorities and with the commander's order? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This pertains to the scope of your duties. And let me just explain for the benefit of the Trial Chamber: Even when men were recruited for JNA units ... let me just say this: Military police units wanted to have only the first category, recruits, meaning the most capable men, and I believe that the document I saw yesterday or the day before spoke about manning of the Sector for Personnel Affairs and that some criteria were not respected when recruitment was carried out.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now look at Chapter 7, entitled "The Security Organs," Article 29, paragraph 9 in that article, which reads: "Expertly directing security organs and the military police in the corps command and units and in other JNA units in the zone of responsibility ..."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question: At the level of the administration, does the security organ expertly direct security bodies in the entire military police and the units that are deployed in the area of Republika Srpska? Thank you?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The answer is yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. For the sake of clarity, let me ask you this: Look at paragraph 14. Skip a few and go to 14. It says here: "Performing other work and tasks prescribed by the Rules of Service of Security Organs and the Armed Forces and other applicable regulations." My question is this: Do you know that those other tasks can also encompass any obligation given to them by a court or a prosecutor's office to collect information about perpetrators of crime that he's duty-bound to investigate, and that they even have to carry out investigations and investigative procedures? Are you aware of that? Is that something you are familiar with from your command practice? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The service had a special book of regulations applicable to the work of the security organs, and these were the only rules that were applied.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In that case, were special training courses organised for military police, soldiers and officers, to teach them their duties? Were such training courses organised for all military police staff, soldiers and officers alike? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I believe that one of the tasks should also read under "directs," that one of the tasks should be training lower levels for security tasks, and that's why training courses are organised, either for security officers or for military policemen and military police units. On the other hand, the other administration organised such training courses for scouts, and that segment was part of the chief of the Administration for Training's duty. He was the one who was supposed to unify all of the training activities.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Look at the clock. We need the second break. We have still some technical problems. At least some of the screens in e-court do not function properly and we are not able to make some highlights. That should be done during the break. But I'd like to raise the question if we would be able to conclude the examination of this witness today. Is that likely, that you may finish, including giving time for the Prosecution for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I believe that we will finish today. We'll do what we planned. And if we can't cover any of the areas with this witness, there will be other officers who will be able to answer the questions that this witness didn't have the time to answer. I'll do my best to finish the cross-examination in keeping with your instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You have only used two hours of your six hours. You should take that into account. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President. And I know General Tolimir wants to allow this person home, but he has also started to hurry, and I would ask that he not have to do that. I did not get into the security and intel branch with this witness. We concentrated on operations. But he, of course, can and has, and I think this witness has an important contribution. But I certainly don't think he should be hurried through it. It's too important. These regulations are too important. And I would -- you know, I hate to bring the witness back, but we can make arrangements to bring him back when it is best for him. It can't be next week because of another witness, but I would say, especially on this important material, if we could slow down, take it easy. I think it's important for you to hear it and for him to be able to fully cross-examine this witness on these topics. Getting into Slovenia, leaving Yugoslavia and things, no. But this particular topic, I really encourage the general to take his full time. It's important for both parties. Most of what I'm hearing, I agree with. We have not charged General Tolimir with being a commander. And so I do have redirect on these issues so you can see where we have some disagreements, but that has opened it up to intel and security. So if we could slow it down. And I think it's just the way it's turned out; unfortunately, I think we're going to need to bring the general back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This would be the position of the Chamber as well. We don't want to put any pressure on you, Mr. Tolimir, to conclude your cross-examination at an earlier time than indicated at the beginning. It is -- what do you think? Is it likely that you will finish today? I don't think so. You indicated you need six hours. And this is also for you a very important witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. He's important for all of us, for you and for me. I respect what you said. He's an expert. I will ask him about everything. And I'm very willing to give time to Mr. McCloskey for his re-examination. I don't want to hassle this witness into coming back again because we can't finish today.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We can't have both, not to bring the witness back and conclude today. I think this is not possible. And, therefore, we should decide not to have an extended sitting. It's very tiring for the witness and for you, Mr. Tolimir, and we have to protect you in that respect. We should have the normal hearing time of today. You should continue your cross-examination after the break, and we will ask the Prosecution to bring the witness back at an appropriate time and to the full convenience of the witness. I think this is the best we can do at the moment.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I think that your previous decision would be better, for us to work longer today for me to finish my cross-examination today and to leave time for the Prosecution for his re-examination. I will, indeed, leave that time to the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is your desire. We will stand by that. We'll have an extended sitting today. We must have our second break now, and we will resume five minutes past 1.00. A little shorter break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Before this break, I asked whether the organs occasionally are tasked by the investigating judge to conduct investigation. Please give us the answer to this question so that we may proceed.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. These are the jobs that are, among others, mentioned in item 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since you mentioned the Rules of Service of the Security Organs of the Armed Forces in which all this is regulated, we'll show these Rules of Service now and ask you about what you know from practice, whereas there will be other witnesses here to testify.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] the document is 65 ter 390. Could we please see it, 65 ter 00390, for the witness to be able to see what I'm asking him about. Could we please see page 5 in Serbian and page 6 in English. In both versions -- can the translation to Serbian be moved. Thank you. And can we now look at bullet point 1, which speaks about the competence of security organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Under 1, we read: "Security organs, as specialised organs of commands, units, institutions, and staffs of the armed forces carry out duties of state security that are placed within their competence by the law and regulations issued pursuant to the law for the purposes of detecting and preventing activities aimed at subverting or disrupting the social order established by the Constitution of the Socialist Federative Republic of Yugoslavia ..." My question: When it comes to this definition of the work of the security organs, isn't it identical to the definition found in the rules on the work of the corps commands, with the only difference being that it covers the entire territory in all the activities of the armed forces? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the definition covers all of the organs in the territory of the state; all of the security organs, that is.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. And can we now look at page 10 in English, page 9 in Serbian, Chapter 2. The title is "Management of Security Organs."

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let's look at bullet point 16, or paragraph 16, and see what it says. We are reading from Chapter 2, "Management of Security Organs," from regulations of the work of the security organs in the armed forces. Paragraph 16 reads: "The security organ is directly subordinated to the commanding officer of the command, unit, institution, or staff of the armed forces in whose strength it is placed in the establishment, and it is responsible to that officer for its work, while JNA security organs in organisations for NVO are responsible to the competent assistant federal secretary for national defence." Thank you. My question: Does this paragraph 16 encompass the work of security organs at all levels and in the entire Yugoslav People's Army, consequently the entire Army of Republika Srpska, which adopted the rules?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this applies to the entire military force.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So does paragraph 16 relate to all organs in all commands, units, and staffs in the armed forces?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but to a lesser extent, and it is applicable only to the level of the unit where they operate.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's look at bullet point 22, where it says, and I quote: "An officer of a security organ, of a command, unit, institution, or staff of the armed forces provides specialist management for a military police unit. He recommends the use of the military police" --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: "... senior officer of a command, unit, institution or staff of the armed forces supervises the work of subordinate security organs according to the general regulations." My question is this: Is it true that all levels of command, an officer in the security organ of those units, institutions, and staffs of the armed forces of the Army of Republika Srpska, control the work of the security organs, according to general regulations? If so, what general regulations are here implied?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These organs control the subordinated security organs, which means that the security organ of the Main Staff controls the security organs in the corps and other units which are tied to the commander of the Main Staff and also in the institutions, within the purview of their own tasks and duties, meaning within the purview of security tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it correct to say "subordinated organs" or "organs in subordinated units"? What is correct? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This refers to security organs in subordinated units and institutions.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In order to be even more precise: Who is the security organ in corps or in the brigade subordinated to? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security organ in the brigade command reports to the brigade commander. A security organ in the corps reports to the corps commander. In battalions and divisions, there was a desk officer for security, and that desk officer reported to the battalion or division commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. While you were brigade commander, did all security organs in your brigade report to you? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did all organs report to you, as commander, while you were a member and commander of that brigade? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And when it comes to the organs from commands superior to your command, did they have only professional and specialised authority over the security organs in your brigade?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let's not go into any further detail of those legal provisions. Let's look at page 22 in Serbian and page --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the page number in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please repeat the page number in English.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Now we are looking at Chapter 4, page 22 in Serbian and page 30 in English.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Page 22. It can't be the same. To which paragraph are you referring?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In English, the page is good; but in Serbian I need Chapter 4. And now we see it at the very bottom of the page, "The Work of Security Organs in War." This is what I wanted, paragraph 85 of Chapter 4.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And I read from that paragraph, where it says: "In war, security organs act in accordance with the provisions of these rules and other rules and regulations that regulate the work of security organs, adapting their own activity, methods, and means of work to the wartime conditions." And then the second passage in the same paragraph reads: "In combat activities, security organs organise and implement measures of counter-intelligence security, and they participate, within the framework of their competence, in the organisation of security measures and the self-protection of commands, units, institutions, and staffs of the armed forces or organisations for NVO ..." My question is this: When we looked at paragraph 85, did we see that security organs in war -- or, rather, in combat activities, organise and implement measures of counter-intelligence, and they, themselves, are not in command? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's how I'm reading this bullet point.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was that also the case in practice? I'm going to repeat the question: Was that the case in practice while you were the commander of the war brigade in that event? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. And was that the common practice in the units of the Army of Republika Srpska, where you later worked and where your work also included your membership in the Main Staff? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please, let's not spend any more time on these regulations, as I've already said. Could you please just listen to an example that I'm going to give you to enable the Trial Chamber to understand all the other things that we didn't talk about. The police organs and the security organs, at every level of command, are they duty-bound to have undergone training, and are they also duty-bound to carry themselves in keeping with the regulations that regulate their obligations? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Officers and non-commissioned officers who were appointed to positions in the security organ or the military police previously had to be trained by attending training courses.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Here's a question: A military police officer, while controlling traffic or checking the ID of any person at Derventa, Han Pijesak, Vlasenica, Belgrade, was he duty-bound to go about the checking of the ID or taking in or arresting a person in the same manner?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A military police officer was duty-bound to do so in accordance with the rules for the -- the rule book of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The Trial Chamber knows the rules in force in the Bratunac Brigade best. The whole military police company had only about 30 or so -- was only about 30-strong, and they carried out all possible duties, traffic control, control of persons, and this and that. Did the commander have to issue an order to a soldier when he checked somebody's ID or controlled traffic or do anything from the remit of the military police organs? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The commander couldn't be present with every military police officer. The military police patrol a place or patrol along an axis, and they carry out their tasks independently.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did the security organ of the Bratunac Brigade then only make proposals to their commander what the military police will do and the commander would issue orders that they would control traffic on this or that road, on a given day, or that they would check the identity documents of persons in a certain area or at certain check-points, and so on, and then they would go execute their duties pursuant to the orders of the commander? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The security organ made proposals to the commander, which is part of the preparation process for the command's decision-making. The commander could either accept the proposal fully or partly. He could also change or amend it. And then the operative officers then transformed that into the commander's orders, pursuant to which the paramilitary [as interpreted] police acted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The commanding of the security organ by the commander then consisted in the commander's taking into consideration the proposals of the security organ and then issuing relevant orders orally or in writing? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Once the commander had heard and adapted or possibly amended the proposal, that would become part of his order through his operative officers, and the commander of the military police would then carry out that order.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Let us now take a look at the military police rule book, which is P01297. Could we please see it, P01297, Chapter 2, on page 9 in Serbian, and it's on page 10 in English. Please rotate the document correctly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I would like to ask you if you are tendering the documents you have used, 65 ter 6903 and 65 ter 00390.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Yes, I seek to tender the documents the Prosecution has introduced through this witness, the one that I have just used in respect of the security organs and one more.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter didn't catch the number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 65 ter 00390.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm not sure if the Prosecution introduced them into the trial. You did it. It is my understanding. Otherwise, we would have already an exhibit number, but we don't. Both documents will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D202 and D203, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you please indicate which D number belongs to which 65 ter number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: 65 ter 6903 is D202, and 65 ter 390 is D203, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, please continue. At a later stage, we should consider which of the diagrams we should receive into evidence. We have now dealt with three of them, but we can postpone a decision on that. Mr. Tolimir, please continue. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think we need to get that number straight. I believe it's 393, not 693.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think the numbers are correct on the screen. 65 ter 6903, that was the rule book we have received at D202. The other one is 65 ter 390, which is now D203.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We'll follow up on that. Hopefully that's correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We're now looking at document P01297, Chapter 2, item 12, page 9 in Serbian and page 10 in English. I'll read out item 12, which is about the command and control of the military police. It says: "The officer in charge of the military unit and institution within whose establishment the military police unit is placed or to which it is attached" --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please slow down. The interpreters didn't catch it.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Bearing in mind what I have just read out from item 12, namely, who has the right to command the military police, tell us, from practice, who commands the military police unit in a brigade, in a corps, or in the Main Staff, respectively. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In brigades, if there -- there can be infantry brigades or motorised brigades. There is a military police unit of the fourth rank, and it's commanded by the brigade commander. In a corps, that's a unit of battalion level and which is commanded by the corps commander. And a military police unit in the Main Staff is commanded by the commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Instead of "fourth rank," it should be "a company."

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I apologise to the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Let us look at item 13, which is about the professional control of the military police. I quote: "With respect to specialty, the officer in charge of the security body of the unit or institution within whose establishment the military police unit is placed or to which it is attached controls the military police. He makes suggestions to the officer in charge of the military unit or institution on the use of military police units and is responsible for the combat readiness of the military police unit and the performance of their tasks." Thank you. End of quote. Who is in charge at any level of command to control the officers in the security units of their level? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This control refers to professional tasks that are exclusively related to the activities of a security or military police. At all command levels, the security organ, from the professional aspect, controls the military police unit with regard to training, enhancing their activities, and the security organ makes proposals to the commander about the use of the military police.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Since different terms appear in the transcript, please tell us if you spoke about "kontrola" or "rukovodjenje." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about "rukovodjenje," which I can also see in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. In that case, I would like it to be recorded in the transcript that you spoke about "rukovodjenje," as is, indeed, stated in item 13 of the rule book of the military police of the armed forces. I didn't want to go into this any deeper. I only asked you, as a professional, a trained professional, to tell us what it was like from your practice in commands at lower levels than yours.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here's my question: If the organs of security and military police, for part of their tasks, carry out their tasks, to who are they responsible, to whom do they report to, and to whom are they subordinate, in a brigade or at the level of the Main Staff? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They report to the commander, starting from the battalion commander, then the security organ in the brigade reports to the brigade commander, the security organ of the corps reports to the corps commander, and the security organ of the Main Staff reports to the Main Staff commander.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's the same when we speak about the services in logistical support or, if in the context of the Main Staff, if we speak about the combat arms organ. The combat arms organ controls the branch units professionally, but they don't have the right to issue orders.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could I just ask for a clarification? Did it say the intel and security organ or the security organ of the Main Staff? Because I wasn't aware that there was a security organ of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, could you please clarify that with the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Obradovic, in your answer, you spoke about organs, and in the transcript we see the term "combat arms organ." Did you speak about that or did you only speak about the security organ of the military police? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I spoke about the security organs of the military police. But at the end I drew a parallel to the services in logistical support as well as the combat arms organs that are part of the staff, because the chiefs of services controlled the services professionally downward. Likewise, the combat arms organs professionally control the branch units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I did not read out the second section of item 13, which is on page 9 in Serbian and page 10 in English, from the rule book of the military police. Let us take a look at this second section of item 13 and if it matches what you have just said. I quote: "When controlling a military --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We need that document on the screen. If I'm not mistaken, this is D202, but I'm not sure about that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We need to look at Chapter 2, item 13. It's about the command and control of the military police. Now we can see it. Let us check the Serbian version. Oh, we need the adequate paragraph in Serbian for the witness as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, is this the right document you want to have on the screen? Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I believe that the previous document was the right one.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Okay. Let's go back to that. But I must confess I'm confused by the numbers now. I would like to ask the Registrar to provide us with the right 65 ter number for the document D202.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is 65 ter 393, not the one that we previously assigned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. And which one is it we now have now on the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: P1297, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Gajic.

utterances.speaker: MR. GAJIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I apologise, I really don't like doing this. However, I should emphasise page 85, line 12; we still find the term "combat arms organs," and that's not what the witness said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is what we heard through the interpreters. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. I think we can all see that part of the problem is we're going too fast. And just on the other topic: Even if the general was to finish now and not to do anything with convoys or any of the other material, which I can't imagine him doing, for me to be able to respond to the security section is going to take more than the time allowed, so I think we should just be realistic at this point; we're just not going to be able to finish today, based on my estimate of how long I will need. Because I know the general, by this time, he can't be anywhere near finished, I don't think. And even if he is, I still would need more time myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Do you know, up to now, the amount of time you will need for re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I would like to have an hour and a half at this point, and that is -- sometimes I'm able to go lesser than that, but at least an hour and a half. But in order to be able to properly find the line and page and make sure everyone's comfortable with that, that takes a fair amount of preparation. I could, you know, punch through it on the fly, which is what -- you know, we do that. But given where we are in the cross-examination, the only -- an hour and a half left, and that we're missing things, numbers are off, I would just prefer that we just slow it down and come back again later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey repeated his proposal from earlier today. What is your position, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. My position is as follows: I still have at least three and a half hours of examination. Everything else I leave to Mr. McCloskey. But I don't want this witness to leave under the warning and the caution that he has been given. I would like him to finish the testimony. If Mr. McCloskey needs another day or two days for his redirect, I'm going to finish right away because I can go through these subject-matters with other witnesses. I think that I should be given at least half an hour more. And then if it's really so important for him, you can give him even more than that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The general has stated he needs three and a half hours, and that's within the time he estimated. For him now to turn that into 30 minutes is not good for the Prosecution. It's not good for anyone. And I, of course, am selfishly looking after my own ability to prepare for my redirect. But to say he needs three and a half hours, which is within his time-frame, and I overtook mine, he should be given that now, for the record. And we -- no one wants keep -- ask the general to come back, but that's just, I think, -- my math tells me there's no other way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It shouldn't go forth and back. We will have our next break now, and we will resume at half past 2.00 for the next session, and we will see how you proceed with your cross-examination. Please bear in mind that you are entitled to have your full time you requested and even some more time because the Prosecution used more time for the examination-in-chief. We adjourn and resume half past 2.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.52 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Tolimir. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I'm about to finish with the topic that we've begun earlier.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you take a look at item 2 under number 13, where it says: "When controlling a military police unit, the officer in charge of the security body from paragraph 1 of this item has the same rights and duties which the officers of arms services, of military units and institutions have in controlling the units of arms and services ." So is it a correct supplement to what you said earlier when you were discussing this item?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. That's the parallel that I mentioned earlier, the parallel with the security organs.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I have one more question about this document. This is the rule book of the military police of the armed forces of SFRY. Does it pertain to all the levels of the military police and the security organs? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does it pertain to all the security organs within the armed forces and within the VRS? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. We took over the legislation from the former JNA.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I don't have any more questions about this document. I have another group of questions to work through, and then I will be able to give more time to Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Yesterday, you were asked about Directive 7 and 7/1, and occasionally 7/6 as well; is that true? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was about the Directives 7 and 7/1.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we now take a look at Directive 7/1, and it is contained within P1199. P1199. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And while we are waiting for it, tell me the following: When a command element is issued, such as a directive or an order, what is the maximum period of validity of such a document? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document ceases to be valid when all the tasks assigned therein are accomplished or a new document is drafted.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The new document, would it also reference the old document and items contained in the old directive if all the tasks have not been accomplished in the meantime? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably the new document is going to contain those tasks which were not accomplished and which were contained in the previous document.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me whether the corps received their tasks in directives, and, more specifically, in which part of the directive? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The tasks are assigned to the corps in the part that pertains to the tasks assigned to their own units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does it mean that each corps receives separate tasks just for itself? Or is it true that general tasks, assigned generally to all the zones, pertain to all the corps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some tasks will be related only to some corps. Some other tasks will be tasks for whose accomplishment it will be necessary to use two or more corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do you remember the Directive 3 from 1993, and then if you bear in mind that all the subsequent directives until 7/1 ensued after the Directive 3, does that mean that something that is not explicitly mentioned in Directive 7/1 is not any more valid if it was mentioned in Directive 3 and it is not mentioned in Directive 7/1? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If a given directive does not contain reformulated tasks from the previous directive, it means that they are not valid anymore.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Just one more thing. When a command act is issued, such as a directive or an order, and when it ceases to be valid, can anybody be held responsible later on for any activity that was assigned, for instance, in document 3; for instance, if we are talking about the corps and the decision pertains to the corps?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand you. Are you talking about the newly-reformulated task in the new directive or not?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I'm talking about a task which is not mentioned in the new directive. An example: If not a single task from Directive 3 or 4 is reformulated in Directive 7 or 7/1, can it be the basis for anybody's responsibility pursuant to Directive 7/1? I'm talking here about the commanders who are assigned tasks by directive 7/1. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: One more question. Yesterday you were asked about Directive 7, page 8 in Serbian, and paragraph 2 was read out aloud to you. You will remember it. It said, In case of UNPROFOR leaving -- do you remember that? In case of UNPROFOR leaving. If you remember that, can you tell us, does that task pertain only to those who have UNPROFOR in their zone or could it also pertain to the corps in whose zones there was no UNPROFOR? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It should be simple enough to get that section up there - it's an important section - so that the witness can fully remember what it said. I can give the -- it's P1214, and it's page 11 in the English. And that should be page, perhaps, 16 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Indeed, this would be helpful for the witness and the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: While we are waiting for this, can you tell us whether you remember the questions that the Prosecutor asked you during the examination-in-chief? And can you also answer the question: Does that task pertain only to those forces within whose zone of responsibility the UNPROFOR units are deployed? Thank you. It's page 15 in Serbian. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And in English?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's the second paragraph, where it says: "In case the UNPROFOR leaves the area of Zepa and Srebrenica, the Drina Corps Command will plan the operation entitled 'Jadar' ..." And so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, does that task pertain only to the Drina Corps or to all the corps within the VRS?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document clearly says that this task pertains to the Drina Corps and the territory within the zone of responsibility of the Drina Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Are you aware that there were certain announcements by the DutchBat that they would want to leave Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: LJUBOMIR OBRADOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for coming here, thank you for everything. I wish that you take part in the ceremony that you have to take part in, in the proper way, and may God bless the deceased person.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I've finished with my part. And I think that Mr. McCloskey, if he wishes to do so, can accomplish his redirect today and we can finish it today. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your efforts, Mr. Tolimir. Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can I just confirm, for the record, that General Tolimir doesn't want to ask him any questions about any of the documents related to convoys that has his initials on it and that material, because this is the only witness that will talk about that. I just want to make sure that there's no rush here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it is very clear from our discussions which are recorded in the transcript that this was the decision of Mr. Tolimir to conclude his cross-examination at this point in time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please commence your re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, this would be -- Mr. President and Your Honours, on direct examination I did not have the witness go into detail about the security branch.
